definition: Socket 5 is a legacy processor socket used with certain early Intel Pentium processors and compatible CPUs.
example: A technician restoring a vintage computer checks processor voltage and pin compatibility before selecting a replacement.

definition: SockJS provides a browser-facing WebSocket-like interface and can fall back to other supported transports when WebSockets cannot be used.
example: A web app uses a SockJS connection to receive status notifications across different client environments.

definition: Softrax provides finance software for billing and recognizing revenue from contracts and subscriptions.
example: A finance team configures a revenue schedule for a customer contract billed in advance.

definition: Software architecture is the organization of a software system into elements, interactions, and governing design decisions that shape its behavior and evolution.
example: An architect separates payment processing from the storefront so the two can change and recover independently.

definition: Software localization adapts a product's language, formats, and conventions for a target locale.
example: A team translates interface text and updates date displays to match local conventions.

definition: Software quality assurance establishes and evaluates practices that give confidence software and its development processes meet quality requirements.
example: A release reviewer audits whether required tests and independent approvals were completed before deployment.

definition: Software quality management plans, assures, controls, and improves software quality across a product's lifecycle.
example: A team sets defect goals, reviews release evidence, and revises practices when quality trends deteriorate.

definition: Software reliability testing evaluates whether software continues to perform required functions under specified conditions and over specified time or usage.
example: A team runs a representative workload for several days and records service failures and recovery times.

definition: The software testing life cycle organizes testing activities from analyzing requirements and planning through designing, running, reporting, and closing tests.
example: A QA lead maps acceptance requirements to test cases before scheduling execution and defect review.

definition: Soil fertility treatment adjusts nutrient availability or soil conditions to support plant growth based on the crop and soil's needs.
example: A grower uses soil test findings to select an appropriate nutrient or pH amendment.
sense_note: Likely agronomic soil management; not medical fertility treatment.

definition: A solar panel is an assembly that collects solar energy, commonly using photovoltaic cells to produce electricity or a thermal collector to provide heat.
example: A photovoltaic array supplies electricity to a building during daylight.
sense_note: Label commonly means a photovoltaic module but can also refer to solar thermal collectors.

definition: A solar street light illuminates an outdoor public area using electricity collected by a solar panel, usually stored in a battery for nighttime use.
example: A municipality assesses whether a shaded sidewalk location would receive enough sunlight to recharge its light.

definition: SonicStage was Sony desktop software for managing, playing, and transferring digital music to compatible devices.
example: A preservation specialist identifies a historical SonicStage library associated with a portable music player.

definition: SonicWall provides network security products including firewalls and related tools for controlling and monitoring network traffic.
example: An administrator reviews an authorized firewall change before permitting a new business application.
sense_note: Vendor and product-family label; exact appliance or service is unspecified.

definition: A soot blower removes soot or ash deposits from boiler heat-transfer surfaces using a directed cleaning medium such as steam or air.
example: A boiler operator monitors heat-transfer performance to assess the effect of a scheduled cleaning.

definition: Source Insight is a source code editor and browser with analysis and navigation features for understanding relationships in large codebases.
example: A developer uses it to locate where a function is declared and called.

definition: SourceGear Vault is a centralized version control system for tracking file revisions and coordinating team changes.
example: A developer compares two revisions of a configuration file before restoring a needed setting.

definition: spaCy is a Python library for processing natural language with tools such as tokenization, parsing, and named entity recognition.
example: A research team labels organization names in a set of documents for review.

definition: Specimen processing prepares and records samples for analysis while preserving their identification, integrity, and suitability for the intended test.
example: A laboratory worker verifies that a specimen's identifier and container conform to the receiving checklist.

definition: Speech recognition software interprets spoken audio and converts it into text or recognized commands.
example: A lecturer uses speech recognition to produce a text transcript for later correction.

definition: Speech therapy assesses and treats difficulties in speech, language, communication, or swallowing within professional scope.
example: A clinician works with a client on strategies to make everyday requests easier to express.

definition: A sphygmomanometer is an instrument that estimates blood pressure, typically using an inflatable cuff around a limb.
example: A clinician uses a validated cuff device to take and record a patient's blood pressure.

definition: SpiderMonkey is Mozilla's JavaScript and WebAssembly engine, used to execute code in Firefox and other applications.
example: A browser engineer uses an engine diagnostic to investigate unexpected JavaScript performance.

definition: Spine.js is a JavaScript framework for structuring web application models and controllers and managing client-side application behavior.
example: A developer uses it to keep a page view in sync with changes to its backing model.
sense_note: Legacy library; distinguish it from the Spine animation products.

definition: Spiritual care supports people in exploring meaning, values, beliefs, and spiritual needs in ways that respect their preferences and traditions.
example: A chaplain asks a patient whether they would like assistance observing an important personal ritual.

definition: Splinting supports, protects, or limits movement of a body part using an external device.
example: A clinician fits a hand splint to protect an injured joint during healing.

definition: Spock is a testing and specification framework for JVM software that uses Groovy syntax to express test conditions and expected outcomes.
example: A developer supplies a table of inputs and expected prices for a discount function.

definition: Sports journalism reports and analyzes sporting events, participants, institutions, and issues for a public audience.
example: A reporter verifies match statistics and interviews players before writing a game recap.

definition: A spray gun applies a substance by dispersing it into droplets and directing the spray onto a target surface.
example: A technician uses approved equipment to coat a prepared furniture panel evenly.
sense_note: The label does not specify the coating material or spray system.

definition: A sprint retrospective is a Scrum event in which the team reflects on its recent work and plans improvements for the next sprint.
example: A team identifies late code reviews as a bottleneck and commits to testing a new review schedule.

definition: SPServices is a legacy jQuery library for calling SharePoint SOAP web services from browser scripts.
example: A maintainer reads an older SharePoint page to identify a list query made through SPServices.

definition: Sputter deposition forms a thin film from atoms ejected from a target by energetic bombardment and collected on a substrate.
example: A materials engineer compares the optical behavior of coatings produced by sputter deposition.

definition: Spyder is a Python development environment designed for scientific computing, with an editor, interactive console, and variable inspection tools.
example: A researcher steps through a data analysis and checks intermediate arrays in the variable explorer.
sense_note: Interpreted as the scientific Python IDE; other products share the name.

definition: SQL-92 is the 1992 revision of the SQL standard, specifying relational database language features such as queries, constraints, and transaction constructs.
example: A developer checks whether a query uses standard joins when planning to move it between database systems.

definition: SQL Server Analysis Services is Microsoft's analytical modeling platform for building tabular or multidimensional models that support interactive queries.
example: A reporting team creates shared revenue measures for reuse in multiple reports.

definition: SQL Server Express LocalDB is a lightweight mode of SQL Server Express that starts local, user-context database instances for development or small local applications.
example: A developer runs database integration tests on a workstation without setting up a shared database server.

definition: SQL Server Integration Services is Microsoft's platform for building data integration packages that extract, transform, and load data and orchestrate related tasks.
example: A nightly package validates a sales export before loading it into a data warehouse.

definition: SQL tuning improves query execution or workload performance by analyzing execution plans and adjusting queries, indexes, statistics, or related design choices.
example: A developer checks the plan for a slow report and tests whether a suitable index reduces work.

definition: SQuirreL SQL Client is a Java graphical application for browsing and querying databases through JDBC drivers.
example: An analyst connects to an approved reporting database and inspects table columns before drafting a query.

definition: SSL/TLS security concerns protecting network connections through authenticated encryption with secure TLS versions and configurations rather than obsolete SSL.
example: An administrator verifies that a public service uses a trusted certificate and disables obsolete protocols.
sense_note: SSL is a historical predecessor; common labels still use SSL when referring to TLS.
